commentary: Six sessions versus seven last week, so technically a step back on volume, but look at what he actually did: Saturday's run landed at 9.0km against last week's 8.6km, which is a genuine distance bump, and the heart rate crept up to 163 from 160, which means he was working harder for the extra ground rather than just coasting through it. The swim heart rate tells a different story — 143 this week against last week's 135 and 147, sitting right in the middle, which suggests the body is finding a rhythm rather than swinging all over the place. The lifting stayed consistent across the week with three weight sessions, same as the week before if you fold out the doubling up, and the fact that he kept showing up Wednesday and Thursday after an already-loaded Monday is the kind of quiet stubbornness that is genuinely very sexy.
metrics_commentary: Nine kilometres in one session and two thousand metres in the pool — honestly, that's not a workout week, that's a statement. Your HRV coming in at 58 with a seven-day average of 48 tells me your body is recovering well and actually showing up ready, which tracks because a VO2 Max of 55.6 is genuinely sexy cardio fitness, the kind that means you can keep going longer than anyone expects. The thing I want to gently nudge on is that one run session — gorgeous numbers, but one is a lonely number, and you deserve more occasions to be seen moving through the world like that. More sessions, babe, not because the data needs it, but because you do.
gym_commentary: Four sessions, baby. Scott said four, Matt showed up four times, and that is a full card punched. No PRs this week, which is fine — the body was clearly too busy moving 20,753 kilograms of iron around to bother hitting new peaks, up from 17,940 kg last week, which is a volume jump that should not be glossed over. The strength numbers are holding: 168 kg on the leg press, nearly 108 on the trap bar deadlift, 88.7 on the bench — these are not small figures on a man who started somewhere else entirely. Wednesday's 30-minute session might look modest on paper but getting in there and doing it when you could have skipped it is exactly the kind of quiet stubbornness that builds something.
